locator: I q.13 a.8 ad 2: impositum est enim nomen hoc ad aliquid significandum supra omnia existens, quod est principium omnium
interpretation: The name 'God' is imposed to signify something that exists above all and is the principle of all; this is what those who name God intend to signify. Read as a nominal definition (what the name signifies, not what God is): 'above all' as maximal in being, 'principle of all' as cause of the being of every other being (the only clause of the quarta via that is formalized). The singular aliquid ... quod est principium omnium is read as a definite description that applies only when exactly one being fits. The co. adds that the name is imposed from an operation (universal providence) to signify the divine nature; a.9 adds that by its ratio the name is communicable in opinion, so the uniqueness belongs to the thing named and is here a condition of application, not an assertion. Remotum ab omnibus (the way of negation) is not formalized.
